title: Tigers Face White Sox in Four-Game Series in Chicago
seoTitle: Tigers vs White Sox: Four-Game Series in Chicago
subtitle: The two teams square off at Rate Field following the Tigers' loss to the Blue Jays
excerpt: The Detroit Tigers arrive in Chicago for a four-game series against the White Sox, featuring starting pitchers Framber Valdez and Erick Fedde.
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
After losing to the Toronto Blue Jays and snapping a six-game winning streak, the Detroit Tigers travel to Chicago to face the White Sox in a four-game series starting Thursday night.

Series opener in Chicago

The first game will be played at Rate Field, starting at 7:40 p.m. (Chicago time). The matchup marks the continuation of the regular season, with the Tigers (72-80) and the White Sox (77-75) looking to improve their standings.

Starting pitchers

For the opener, the Tigers put left-handed pitcher Framber Valdez on the mound, who comes in with 13 innings without allowing an earned run this month and a 4.01 ERA on the season. On the Chicago side, right-hander Erick Fedde takes the start, presenting a 3.97 ERA and having recorded two recent starts with a 2.57 ERA over 28 innings.

White Sox lineup against Valdez

Against Valdez, the White Sox set up a predominantly right-handed batting order. Chase Meidroth leads off, followed by Tommy Pham in the second spot, despite it being considered an unusual move. The rest of the lineup includes Miguel Vargas, Randal Grichuk, Munetaka Murakami, Brenton Doyle, Jake Rogers, Luisangel Acuña (replacing Colson Montgomery, who left injured), and Braden Montgomery in right field.

Recent performance of Fedde and Valdez

Fedde has been a mainstay in the White Sox rotation, pitching at least five innings in his last three appearances and maintaining a 2.57 ERA in his two starts over the last seven. Valdez, who had a rough start in Detroit, records a 2.91 ERA over his last seven games, demonstrating greater control and efficiency in generating ground balls.

Expectations for the series

With Valdez seeking to consolidate his improvement and Fedde trying to maintain his consistency, the series promises to be competitive. The choice of Pham in the second spot of the lineup indicates the White Sox manager's confidence in his firepower, while the Tigers will rely on Valdez's experience to contain the opposing offense.

With information from Bless You Boys, Sports Illustrated.
